summary.headline: Veranda FY26 revenue rose 35% to INR 482 crore and PAT turned positive at INR 130 crore; FY27 guidance is INR 670 crore revenue and INR 144 crore PAT.
summary.overview: Management reported Q4 FY26 revenue of INR 132 crore (up 52% YoY) and FY26 EBITDA of about INR 204 crore (up 135%). FY26 PAT of INR 130 crore compares with a loss of about INR 252 crore in FY25, and this was the fifth consecutive PAT-positive quarter. Management said FY26 guidance was broadly achieved, with non-commerce well ahead and commerce broadly in line. The J.K. Shah Commerce Education demerger is awaiting final NCLT approval, with listing targeted for end-July or mid-August 2026. FY27 guidance is revenue of about INR 670 crore and PAT above INR 144 crore.

financial_highlights.change: vs loss of INR 252 crore in FY25

financial_highlights.value: 2.5 lakh students; collections nearly INR 449 crore

financial_highlights.change: Q4 loss of about INR 3 crore; segment EBITDA positive INR 2 crore for the year

segments.name: Commerce (to be demerged as J.K. Shah Commerce Education Ltd)
segments.commentary: Performed broadly in line with expectations in FY26; FY26 revenue is about INR 300-330 crore, with Tapasya contributing about INR 70 crore. Management expects FY27 EBITDA of INR 180-185 crore and a long-term target of INR 1,000 crore-plus revenue by FY30.

segments.name: Non-commerce (government test prep and academic/K-12)
segments.commentary: Significantly outperformed estimates on government test prep traction and operational improvements. Government test prep posted a Q4 loss of about INR 3 crore after a one-time INR 5 crore impairment; the segment otherwise earned INR 2 crore EBITDA for the year.

segments.name: Vocational (divested to SNVA Veranda, 50% associate)
segments.commentary: Divested into a joint structure with SNVA; Veranda accounts for 50% of SNVA's consolidated profit as an associate, not line-by-line. A North American entity remains in continuing operations (about INR 51 crore segment revenue) and is planned for eventual sale subject to RBI approvals.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target of about INR 670 crore, about 40% growth YoY.
FY27 PAT projected at over INR 144 crore (CEO said over INR 140 crore in closing).
Commerce FY27 EBITDA expected at INR 180-185 crore; management flagged a minor EBITDA margin dip in commerce from opening about 15 new colleges.
Demerger: NCLT hearing on June 3, 2026; final order expected about 30 days later; listing targeted by end-July or mid-August 2026.
Allocation of assets between the two entities is expected at about 35:65 (Veranda : J.K. Shah) on net assets, subject to the appointment date.
Commerce to reach INR 1,000 crore-plus revenue by FY30.
Managed B.Com colleges to roughly double in FY27 versus March 2026; B.Com enrollment expected at 19,000-plus versus 17,000 last year (about 15% growth).
capex_capacity: Plan to add about 15 new B.Com/commerce colleges (managed portfolio) in FY27 across North and West India, versus 15-17 colleges currently.
Government test prep expansion into Karnataka in FY27, aiming to be the number one player in South India including Telangana and Andhra Pradesh.
Academic segment: evaluating managed pre-KG schools and expanding managed K-12 schools.

New college investment is front-loaded: lease deposits and soft capex (furniture, digital dashboards) in year one, with faculty and marketing expensed; the first year is expected to be marginally breakeven before cash flow.
Commerce Virtuals launched for Class 11-12 students; Group 1 offline, junior IAS and magazine subscription offerings added in government test prep.
demand_pricing: Commerce admissions demand is strong: Chennai B.Com colleges reportedly see about 1:70 applicant-to-seat ratio, per an individual investor's question.
Management said fees rise about 5-10% annually, just ahead of inflation.
Managed college revenue collected by colleges is about INR 80-90 crore.

SNVA Veranda: university-led growth; online applications from 64 countries; owns university assets in the U.S., and affiliated colleges in the U.K., Switzerland and Europe, with potential additions in Italy and Singapore.
Management flagged challenges: lower CA pass percentages, changes in the number of exams held per year, site selection and faculty hiring at scale.

qa_highlights.question: When will the J.K. Shah demerger list, and how will the listing unlock value?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the NCLT hearing is on June 3, 2026, with the final order about 30 days later, then ROC filings and listing approvals; listing is expected by end-July or mid-August 2026. Management said the standalone commerce business is sharply focused and expected to carry a higher valuation multiple.

qa_highlights.question: Why does a vocational-division revenue of INR 51 crore still appear in consolidated results?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said one North American entity was not hived off with the divestment and remains with the non-commerce business; it is planned for eventual sale subject to RBI approvals.

qa_highlights.question: Why was there a Q4 loss in government test prep, and are there further impairments?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a one-time INR 5 crore impairment was taken in Q4 following audit testing; the segment otherwise earned INR 2 crore EBITDA for the year. Management said goodwill and intangibles were tested and no further impairment was taken in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: How will the warrants issued for the BB Virtuals and Navkar acquisitions be treated on demerger?
qa_highlights.answer: About 75% of the warrants are yet to be subscribed, with the deadline in August 2026. If demerger happens before then, warrants will be split proportionately between the two entities on the same asset ratio, per the scheme.

qa_highlights.question: Why will FY27 commerce EBITDA margin dip about 4-5%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the dip to front-loaded opex for about 15 new colleges. Lease deposits and soft capex are capitalised in year one, while faculty and marketing are expensed; the first year is expected to be marginally breakeven, with benefits from year two.

qa_highlights.question: What is the reinvestment plan for surplus cash after debt repayment and demerger?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cash will fund commerce geographic expansion across all districts and new products including 11th-12th education, and non-commerce expansion in Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh and Telangana, plus managed pre-KG and K-12 schools.

risks_watch: Demerger timing: NCLT final order and SEBI/exchange listing approvals; any slippage beyond July-August 2026.
Warrant overhang: about 75% of warrants remain to be subscribed before the August 2026 deadline.
Commerce margin dip in FY27 from the college expansion; watch whether the new colleges breakeven in year one as guided.
Operating risks flagged by management: lower CA pass rates, changes in exam frequency, site selection and faculty availability.
Asset allocation of about 35:65 between the entities is provisional and depends on the appointment date.
Possible further one-time charges; management said no further impairment was taken in FY26.
summary.management_tone: Confident on FY26 delivery and FY27 targets, with clear timelines on the demerger. Evasive on the valuation split and the exact allocation of the commerce and non-commerce entities, saying figures will be set on the appointment date.
key_quotes: Importantly, we remain committed to the guidance shared with investors at the beginning of the year and successfully delivered largely in line with our stated expectations.
Veranda reported its first full year PAT-positive performance since listing with a PAT of INR130 crores compared to a loss of over INR250 crores in FY25.
So the first year is an investment, which obviously we are taking charge on our P&L.
The future benefits of this is what is driving us to deliver potentially a INR 1,000 crores plus revenue for FY '30.

growth.why: FY27 guidance of about INR 670 crore revenue (~40% growth) and PAT over INR 144 crore, backed by roughly doubling managed B.Com colleges (about 15 new), Karnataka expansion, B.Com enrollment guided to 19,000+ (~15%), and fee increases of 5-10% a year; specific college count is given but no firm order book or contracted capacity figures were shown for the revenue step-up.
